description: Explicit iterative successor search through a bounded path of nested sorted catalogs, with bridge ranks and a weighted result checksum.

source.title: Fractional Cascading: I. A Data Structuring Technique
source.application_paper: Fractional Cascading: II. Applications, Algorithmica 1, 163-191, DOI 10.1007/BF01840441
source.copyright: The papers are copyrighted publications; this package uses their algorithm description and contains independently written code.

input.encoding: [m, q, (catalog_size, sorted_catalog_keys...) repeated m times, query_keys...]
input.catalog_rules: Each catalog is strictly increasing; every catalog after the first is a subset of its predecessor.

output.meaning: For query j and catalog i, let successor be the least catalog key >= query, or sentinel 34 if none exists; code a found key as key+17. Return sum((j+1)*(i+1)*code) using zero-based j and i.

algorithm_details.profile_scope: A deterministic nested-catalog path specialization of fractional cascading. The profile does not claim the full arbitrary catalog-graph construction, high-degree handling, range-restricted edges, or dynamic updates.
algorithm_details.primary: Build one bridge table per adjacent catalog pair. For each lower-bound slot in a parent catalog, store the matching lower-bound slot in the child catalog. Because child keys are a subset of parent keys, the child's lower bound for any query in that parent gap equals the bridge target. For each query, binary-search the first catalog once, then follow one bridge per path edge.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Perform an independent lower-bound search in every original catalog for every query and compute the same weighted checksum.
algorithm_details.query_complexity: O(log n0 + m) per query, where n0 is the first catalog size and m is the number of catalogs; output checksum processing is O(m).
algorithm_details.call_complexity: O(sum(n_i) + q*(log n0 + m)) time and O(sum(n_i) + 17*(m-1)) bounded scratch, including bridge construction.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Catalog keys are unique and strictly increasing. A successor is the first key greater than or equal to the query. Query order and catalog order are preserved; no successor uses the distinct sentinel 34.
